# XY Forever serial protocol 1.33: library commands

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.33](../PROTOCOL.md).

### 0x40 `library.set_default`

Make a library entry the default firmware. An entry whose content is not installed (listed as content not installed) first gets its content: B starts the
content switch as a job and answers `started` (`job.status`: phase `inputs`, `content` with done/total in files, `finish` while it writes the record and the
default; `done` with detail = the id once the default is written; `failed` leaves the default unchanged, `error` 15 with code 1 when `/yaffs2/content/` is not
the official set, 2 when the entry would replace an official file; a cut or failure leaves the content state switching, which nothing boots from until this
request runs again). A build without the switch answers `no_content` (nothing sent to A). Processor A finds the one entry whose id has this hash and an
`os.ldr`, and writes the next of the two state files (`/yaffs2/xy-forever/state-a.txt`, `state-b.txt`). ok means A finished and the menu shows the new default;
`storage` means the menu's default did not change. Tools can confirm by reading both state files: the valid one with the higher `seq=` holds `default=ID`.

| Request field (2 to 32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated (the folder name under `/yaffs2/xy-forever/firmware/`) |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id_hash` | u32 | CRC-32 of the id bytes, as sent to processor A (0 for `bad_request`) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `link`, `storage`, `no_content`, `started`. Tool timeout: 75 s. **Destructive**: ask
the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_SET_DEFAULT`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.0.

### 0x41 `tfw.check`

Check that a firmware package on the device is official and that the device's own keys open it. Processor B reads the package header, verifies its P-224
signature with the public key in the device's one-time-programmable memory (OTP), then checks that the AES key there decrypts the package's name block and ZIP
directory. It reads nothing else and changes nothing; the keys are read only for a well-formed header and nothing derived from them is sent. A cut (16-byte
header: u32 `0x54434658`, package bytes, head bytes, tail offset; then the package's first head bytes and its bytes from the tail offset on) is checked as the
package. ok: the check ran (see `verdict`); an error: the file could not be read.

| Request field (10 to 240 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/` of a `.tfw` file or a cut of one, NUL-terminated |

| Reply field, after the status (40 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `verdict` | u32 | 0 = pass; 1 = fail. The result |
| `reason` | u32 | 0 = pass; 1 = a read failed; 2 = not a package, or its sizes differ from the file; 3 = an AES key index other than 0; 4 = the device's one-time-programmable memory gave no key; 5 = the device's public key is not on the curve; 6 = the signature does not verify; 7 = the device's key does not decrypt the package; 8 = the decrypted ZIP directory is malformed. Why |
| `public_key_sha256` | bytes[32] | SHA-256 of the device's 56-byte public key; zero when none was read |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `range`. Tool timeout: 60 s. Build switch `XYF_TFW_CHECK` (on in
product builds; without it: `unsupported`). Since 1.2.

### 0x43 `library.boot`

Boot a library entry once, as PLAY on it in the library menu. After the ok reply the menu closes, USB goes away and the entry boots once; the default and the
state files do not change. Errors boot nothing: an entry the menu does not list is `not_found`, one it lists without an `os.ldr` (not selectable there) `state`,
one whose content is not installed `no_content` (make it the default to install its content), a lost link `link`.

| Request field (34 to 64 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the id bytes, without the NUL |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`, `sha`, `link`, `not_found`, `state`, `no_content`. Tool timeout: 30 s. Since 1.7.
